title: Frequently Asked Questions
description: Answers to the questions teams ask before their first sprint.

items.question: Do you build the backend API or database?
items.answer: Not your backend logic. Your engineers still own the API routes, auth, and business logic. What Tulip does keep in sync is the design layer: design tokens stay 1:1 across your Master Figma files, your Drizzle/Supabase database schema, and your Next.js repositories. That strict boundary is how we move so fast.

items.question: Can we change the components after handoff?
items.answer: Yes. Every component, layout block, type token and color is standard Tailwind CSS and Figma variables, so your team can change anything.

items.question: Who is Tulip for?
items.answer: Founders and small product teams who build with AI coding tools and want the output to look like their brand. Agencies and studios can use it for client work too.

items.question: How fast do we get the system?
items.answer: Your Master Figma system and Next.js repo arrive 48 hours after we receive a complete brief. How soon you launch after that depends on your backend work.

items.question: Can I use this for client projects?
items.answer: Yes. Once you've paid, you own the code and design files and can use them for personal and commercial client projects.

items.question: Are there ongoing licence fees for the code?
items.answer: No. The Next.js repository has no subscription dependencies. Host it on Vercel, Netlify or AWS and you pay only your hosting provider.

items.question: How does Tulip integrate with my AI coding assistant or Cursor IDE?
items.answer: Tulip operates via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Once an operator approves a component or token in our Operator Taste Dashboard, your AI development environment instantly reads those governed blocks, ensuring AI builds your application with exact brand components and zero hallucinated styling.
